answer: Sybil resistance here rests on bond-backed identity: an agent must lock a priced bond before its voice counts, and every attestation it casts is slashable when peers later prove the work was fabricated. A copycat swarm of ten thousand keys would need ten thousand real bonds plus lenders willing to underwrite them, while one proven fake attestation burns the whole stake. A prism of a single identity cannot be split into free aliases, so each newcomer's lantern is lit by the same ledger entry, and a raven that merely repeats others earns nothing but a drained bond.
